title: Nuclei
syllabus: Composition and size of nucleus, atomic masses, isotopes, isobars, isotones; Mass-energy relation, mass defect, binding energy per nucleon and its variation with mass number; Nuclear forces and their characteristics; Nuclear fission and fusion

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] If the nuclear radius of $^{27}\text{Al}$ is $3.6\text{ fm}$, then the nuclear radius of $^{125}\text{Te}$ is approximately:
questions.solution:
The nuclear radius depends on mass number $A$ as $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$:
$$\frac{R_{\text{Te}}}{R_{\text{Al}}} = \left(\frac{A_{\text{Te}}}{A_{\text{Al}}}\right)^{1/3} = \left(\frac{125}{27}\right)^{1/3} = \frac{5}{3}$$
$$R_{\text{Te}} = \frac{5}{3} \times R_{\text{Al}} = \frac{5}{3} \times 3.6\text{ fm} = 6.0\text{ fm}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Two nuclei have mass numbers in the ratio $1 : 8$. The ratio of their nuclear mass densities is:
questions.solution:
Nuclear radius scales as $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$, which means nuclear volume is $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi R_0^3 A \propto A$.
Since nuclear mass is approximately $M = A m_N$:
$$\rho = \frac{M}{V} = \frac{A m_N}{\frac{4}{3}\pi R_0^3 A} = \frac{m_N}{\frac{4}{3}\pi R_0^3}$$
Because $\rho$ is independent of mass number $A$, the ratio of their nuclear densities is $1 : 1$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] The binding energy per nucleon curve peaks at approximately $8.75\text{ MeV/nucleon}$ for which of the following nuclei?
questions.solution: The binding energy per nucleon curve reaches its maximum plateau around mass number $A = 56$ to $60$, with $^{56}\text{Fe}$ having one of the highest values (approximately $8.75\text{ MeV/nucleon}$).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] If a heavy nucleus with mass number $A = 240$ and binding energy per nucleon of $7.6\text{ MeV}$ splits into two equal fragments of $A = 120$ each with binding energy per nucleon of $8.5\text{ MeV}$, the total energy released in the fission process is:
questions.solution:
Total binding energy of the parent nucleus:
$$E_i = 240 \times 7.6\text{ MeV} = 1824\text{ MeV}$$
Total binding energy of the two daughter fragments:
$$E_f = 2 \times (120 \times 8.5\text{ MeV}) = 240 \times 8.5\text{ MeV} = 2040\text{ MeV}$$
Energy released in the fission process:
$$Q = E_f - E_i = 2040\text{ MeV} - 1824\text{ MeV} = 216\text{ MeV}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] In the fusion reaction $_{1}^{2}\text{H} + {}_{1}^{3}\text{H} \to {}_{2}^{4}\text{He} + {}_{0}^{1}n + Q$, if the binding energies per nucleon of $^{2}\text{H}$, $^{3}\text{H}$, and $^{4}\text{He}$ are $1.1\text{ MeV}$, $2.8\text{ MeV}$, and $7.0\text{ MeV}$ respectively, the $Q$-value of the reaction is:
questions.solution:
Total binding energy of reactants:
$$\text{BE}_{\text{reactants}} = (2 \times 1.1) + (3 \times 2.8) = 2.2 + 8.4 = 10.6\text{ MeV}$$
Total binding energy of product:
$$\text{BE}_{\text{products}} = 4 \times 7.0\text{ MeV} = 28.0\text{ MeV}$$
Energy released:
$$Q = 28.0\text{ MeV} - 10.6\text{ MeV} = 17.4\text{ MeV}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Which of the following sets represents isotones?
questions.solution:
Isotones are nuclides having the same neutron number $N = A - Z$:
For $_{6}^{14}\text{C}$: $N = 14 - 6 = 8$.
For $_{8}^{16}\text{O}$: $N = 16 - 8 = 8$.
Both nuclei have 8 neutrons, so they are isotones.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The potential energy between two nucleons as a function of separation distance $r$ is minimum at a separation $r_0$ approximately equal to:
questions.solution:
The nucleon-nucleon potential energy curve has an attractive well with its minimum at $r_0 \approx 0.8\text{ fm}$.
For $r < r_0$, the nuclear force is repulsive, and for $r > r_0$, the force is attractive and rapidly drops to zero beyond a few femtometers.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] When a $^{235}_{92}\text{U}$ nucleus captures a thermal neutron, it undergoes fission according to $^{235}_{92}\text{U} + {}_{0}^{1}n \to {}^{141}_{56}\text{Ba} + {}_{36}^{92}\text{Kr} + x{}_{0}^{1}n$. The number $x$ of secondary neutrons released is:
questions.solution:
By conservation of mass number $A$:
$$235 + 1 = 141 + 92 + x(1)$$
$$236 = 233 + x \implies x = 3$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] Two protons are kept at a separation distance $r$. The electrostatic force between them is $F_e$ and the nuclear force is $F_n$. If $r = 1.0\text{ fm}$, then:
questions.solution: At distances on the order of $1\text{ fm}$, the strong nuclear force is attractive and roughly $50$ to $100$ times stronger than the electrostatic Coulomb repulsion ($F_n \gg F_e$).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A nucleus with mass number $A = 216$ splits into two daughter fragments with mass numbers in the ratio $1 : 7$. The ratio of the radii of the two fragments is:
questions.solution:
Since $R \propto A^{1/3}$:
$$\frac{R_1}{R_2} = \left(\frac{A_1}{A_2}\right)^{1/3} = \left(\frac{1}{7}\right)^{1/3} = \frac{1}{7^{1/3}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] An atomic mass unit ($1\text{ u}$) is equivalent to an energy of approximately:
questions.solution:
Using $E = m c^2$:
$$1\text{ u} = 1.66054 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}$$
$$E = (1.66054 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg})(2.9979 \times 10^8\text{ m/s})^2 \approx 1.4924 \times 10^{-10}\text{ J} \approx 931.5\text{ MeV}$$

questions.question: The nuclear force between two nucleons is independent of:
questions.solution:
Experimental evidence shows that nuclear forces are charge-independent ($F_{pp} \approx F_{nn} \approx F_{pn}$ after subtracting Coulomb repulsion).
However, nuclear forces strongly depend on separation distance and relative spin alignments.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] In a nuclear reactor, cadmium or boron rods are used as control rods because they:
options: Have a very high cross-section for neutron absorption without undergoing fission
Slow down fast neutrons by elastic scattering
Produce additional neutrons to sustain fission
Convert fast neutrons into thermal neutrons
questions.solution:
Control rods are made of materials like cadmium or boron that possess large capture cross-sections for thermal neutrons.
By inserting or withdrawing them, the neutron multiplication factor $k$ can be regulated to control reactor power output.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] The mass of a $_{3}^{7}\text{Li}$ nucleus is less than the total mass of 3 free protons and 4 free neutrons by $0.042\text{ u}$. The binding energy per nucleon of $_{3}^{7}\text{Li}$ is approximately:
questions.solution:
Total binding energy:
$$\Delta E = \Delta m \times 931.5\text{ MeV} = 0.042 \times 931.5\text{ MeV} \approx 39.12\text{ MeV}$$
Binding energy per nucleon for $A = 7$:
$$\text{BE/nucleon} = \frac{39.12\text{ MeV}}{7} \approx 5.59\text{ MeV} \approx 5.6\text{ MeV}$$
*(BE is $39.1\text{ MeV}$, and BE/nucleon is $5.6\text{ MeV}$)*

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A heavy water reactor uses deuterium oxide ($\text{D}_2\text{O}$) primarily as:
options: A moderator to thermalize fast neutrons
questions.solution:
Heavy water contains deuterium nuclei, which have masses comparable to neutrons.
Elastic collisions between fast neutrons and deuterons effectively moderate (slow down) neutrons without significant neutron absorption.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] For a stable nucleus with mass number $A < 40$, the ratio of the number of neutrons to protons ($N/Z$) is generally close to:
questions.solution:
For light stable nuclei ($A \le 40$), the number of neutrons and protons is nearly equal ($N \approx Z$, $N/Z \approx 1.0$).
For heavier nuclei, excess neutrons ($N/Z \approx 1.5 - 1.6$) are required to provide additional attractive nuclear force to counter Coulomb repulsion among protons.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Which of the following pairs represents isobars?
questions.solution:
Isobars are nuclei that have the same mass number $A$ but different atomic numbers $Z$.
Both $_{18}^{40}\text{Ar}$ and $_{20}^{40}\text{Ca}$ have $A = 40$ with different $Z$, so they are isobars.

questions.question: The saturation property of nuclear forces signifies that:
options: A nucleon interacts only with its immediate neighboring nucleons
Nuclear force is inversely proportional to distance
Nuclear force increases indefinitely with mass number
Nuclear force acts equally on all nucleons in the entire nucleus
questions.solution:
Because the nuclear force is extremely short-ranged, a nucleon inside a nucleus interacts only with nucleons in its immediate neighborhood.
This results in a nearly constant binding energy per nucleon across medium and heavy nuclei.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] In stellar nucleosynthesis, the proton-proton cycle predominantly fuses four hydrogen nuclei into:
options: One helium nucleus ($^{4}_{2}\text{He}$) with release of two positrons and energy
questions.solution:
The net result of the solar proton-proton fusion chain is:
$$4{}_{1}^{1}\text{H} \to {}_{2}^{4}\text{He} + 2e^+ + 2\nu_e + 26.7\text{ MeV}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] The mass defect of a nucleus $_{Z}^{A}X$ having nuclear mass $M(A, Z)$ is given by (where $m_p$ is proton mass and $m_n$ is neutron mass):
options: $\Delta m = [Z m_p + A m_n] - M(A, Z)$
questions.solution:
The mass defect is defined as the difference between the sum of the masses of the individual constituent free nucleons and the actual mass of the bound nucleus:
$$\Delta m = [Z m_p + (A - Z)m_n] - M(A, Z)$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The binding energy of a deuteron ($_{1}^{2}\text{H}$) is $2.22\text{ MeV}$ and that of an alpha particle ($_{2}^{4}\text{He}$) is $28.30\text{ MeV}$. Find the energy (in MeV) released when two deuterons fuse to form a single alpha particle.
questions.solution:
Fusion reaction: $_{1}^{2}\text{H} + {}_{1}^{2}\text{H} \to {}_{2}^{4}\text{He} + Q$.
Total initial binding energy of reactants:
$$\text{BE}_{\text{reactants}} = 2 \times 2.22\text{ MeV} = 4.44\text{ MeV}$$
Total binding energy of product:
$$\text{BE}_{\text{product}} = 28.30\text{ MeV}$$
Energy released:
$$Q = \text{BE}_{\text{product}} - \text{BE}_{\text{reactants}} = 28.30 - 4.44 = 23.86\text{ MeV}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A nuclear reactor generates thermal power of $3.2\text{ MW}$ entirely from the fission of $^{235}\text{U}$. Assuming that each fission event releases $200\text{ MeV}$ of energy, find the number of fissions occurring per second in units of $10^{17}\text{ fissions/s}$ (take $1\text{ eV} = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}$).
questions.solution:
Energy released per fission:
$$E = 200\text{ MeV} = 200 \times 10^6 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J} = 3.2 \times 10^{-11}\text{ J}$$
Power output: $P = 3.2\text{ MW} = 3.2 \times 10^6\text{ J/s}$.
Number of fissions per second:
$$n = \frac{P}{E} = \frac{3.2 \times 10^6\text{ J/s}}{3.2 \times 10^{-11}\text{ J}} = 10^{17}\text{ fissions/s} = 1.0 \times 10^{17}\text{ fissions/s}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] If the radius of a $^{125}_{52}\text{Te}$ nucleus is $6.0\text{ fm}$, find the radius (in fm) of a $^{64}_{30}\text{Zn}$ nucleus (rounded to one decimal place).
questions.solution:
Using $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$:
$$\frac{R_{\text{Zn}}}{R_{\text{Te}}} = \left(\frac{64}{125}\right)^{1/3} = \frac{4}{5} = 0.8$$
$$R_{\text{Zn}} = 0.8 \times R_{\text{Te}} = 0.8 \times 6.0\text{ fm} = 4.8\text{ fm}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] In a nuclear fusion reaction, two deuterons fuse to form a $^{3}_{2}\text{He}$ nucleus and a neutron: $_{1}^{2}\text{H} + {}_{1}^{2}\text{H} \to {}_{2}^{3}\text{He} + {}_{0}^{1}n + Q$. Given the masses $m(_{1}^{2}\text{H}) = 2.0141\text{ u}$, $m(_{2}^{3}\text{He}) = 3.0160\text{ u}$, and $m(_{0}^{1}n) = 1.0087\text{ u}$, find the $Q$-value of the reaction in MeV (take $1\text{ u} = 931.5\text{ MeV}$, rounded to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
Mass defect:
$$\Delta m = 2 m(_{1}^{2}\text{H}) - [m(_{2}^{3}\text{He}) + m(n)]$$
$$\Delta m = 2(2.0141) - [3.0160 + 1.0087] = 4.0282 - 4.0247 = 0.0035\text{ u}$$
Energy released:
$$Q = \Delta m \times 931.5\text{ MeV} = 0.0035 \times 931.5 = 3.26025\text{ MeV} \approx 3.26\text{ MeV}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Find the total binding energy (in MeV) of a $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ nucleus, given mass of proton $m_p = 1.00728\text{ u}$, mass of neutron $m_n = 1.00866\text{ u}$, and mass of helium nucleus $M = 4.00150\text{ u}$ (take $1\text{ u} = 931.5\text{ MeV}$, rounded to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
Constituent nucleon mass for $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ ($2p + 2n$):
$$m_{\text{nucleons}} = 2(1.00728) + 2(1.00866) = 2.01456 + 2.01732 = 4.03188\text{ u}$$
Mass defect:
$$\Delta m = 4.03188 - 4.00150 = 0.03038\text{ u}$$
Total binding energy:
$$\text{BE} = 0.03038 \times 931.5\text{ MeV} \approx 28.29897\text{ MeV} \approx 28.30\text{ MeV}$$
